subjective.question: A car moving with a constant acceleration of 3 m/s² passes a point A with a speed of 6 m/s. Find the distance travelled by the car after 8 seconds.
subjective.answer: Here u = 6 m/s, a = 3 m/s² and t = 8 s. Using s = ut + ½at²: s = 6(8) + ½(3)(8²) = 48 + 96 = 144 m.

subjective.question: State the equations of motion for a particle moving in a straight line with constant acceleration, defining every symbol used.
subjective.answer: The equations are: (i) v = u + at (ii) s = ut + ½at² (iii) v² = u² + 2as (iv) s = ½(u + v)t where u = initial velocity, v = final velocity, a = constant acceleration, s = displacement and t = time.

subjective.question: The displacement of a particle moving in a straight line is given by s = t³ − 6t² + 9t metres. Find its velocity and acceleration at t = 2 s, and find the times at which the particle is instantaneously at rest.
subjective.answer: v = ds/dt = 3t² − 12t + 9 and a = dv/dt = 6t − 12. At t = 2 s: v = 3(4) − 12(2) + 9 = −3 m/s, so the particle is moving at 3 m/s in the negative direction, and a = 6(2) − 12 = 0. The particle is instantaneously at rest when v = 0: 3t² − 12t + 9 = 0 ⇒ t² − 4t + 3 = 0 ⇒ (t − 1)(t − 3) = 0, so t = 1 s and t = 3 s.

subjective.question: A stone is thrown vertically upwards with a speed of 20 m/s. Taking g = 10 m/s², find the maximum height reached and the time taken to reach it.
subjective.answer: At the maximum height v = 0. Using v² = u² − 2gs with u = 20 m/s and g = 10 m/s²: 0 = 400 − 20s ⇒ s = 20 m. Using v = u − gt: 0 = 20 − 10t ⇒ t = 2 s. The total time of flight is 2 × 2 = 4 s.

subjective.question: If the mass of a body is 2 kg, find the gravitational force acting on the body in the earth's gravitational field.
subjective.answer: The gravitational force on a body is its weight, W = mg. Here m = 2 kg and g = 9.8 m/s², so: W = 2 × 9.8 = 19.6 N.

subjective.question: State Newton's three laws of motion.
subjective.answer: First law: A body remains at rest, or in uniform motion in a straight line, unless acted upon by a resultant external force. Second law: The rate of change of momentum of a body is proportional to the resultant force acting on it and takes place in the direction of the force; for constant mass, F = ma. Third law: To every action there is an equal and opposite reaction.

subjective.question: A force of 20 N acts on a body of mass 5 kg, initially at rest on a smooth horizontal surface. Find the acceleration of the body and the distance travelled in 4 seconds.
subjective.answer: By Newton's second law, F = ma, so a = F/m = 20/5 = 4 m/s². Starting from rest, the distance travelled in 4 s is: s = ut + ½at² = 0 + ½(4)(4²) = 32 m.

subjective.question: Classify the following quantities as vectors or scalars: force, mass, velocity, density, speed, momentum.
subjective.answer: Vector quantities (having both magnitude and direction): force, velocity, momentum. Scalar quantities (having magnitude only): mass, density, speed.

subjective.question: Define power. A force of 50 N acts on a body moving with a velocity of 4 m/s in the direction of the force. Find the power developed.
subjective.answer: Power is the rate of doing work: P = dW/dt. For a constant force F acting on a body moving with velocity v in the direction of the force, P = Fv. Here F = 50 N and v = 4 m/s, so: P = 50 × 4 = 200 W.

subjective.question: Define work and kinetic energy. A body of mass 2 kg moves with a speed of 3 m/s; find its kinetic energy, and state the work–energy principle.
subjective.answer: The work done by a constant force is the product of the force and the distance moved in its direction: W = Fs. The kinetic energy of a body of mass m moving with speed v is KE = ½mv². Here KE = ½(2)(3²) = 9 J. Work–energy principle: the work done by the resultant force acting on a body is equal to the change in its kinetic energy.

subjective.question: A particle moves in a straight line with simple harmonic motion. The amplitude of the motion is 0.5 m and the particle passes the centre of oscillation O with a speed of 2 m/s. Calculate the speed of the particle P when OP = 0.2 m.
subjective.answer: For SHM, v² = ω²(a² − x²), where a is the amplitude. The speed is greatest at the centre (x = 0), so: ω = (maximum speed)/a = 2/0.5 = 4 rad/s. When x = OP = 0.2 m: v = 4√(0.5² − 0.2²) = 4√(0.25 − 0.04) = 4√0.21 ≈ 1.83 m/s.

subjective.question: A particle moves with simple harmonic motion described by x = a cos(ωt). Show that v² = ω²(a² − x²), and state the maximum speed and the maximum acceleration of the particle.
subjective.answer: Differentiating x = a cos(ωt) gives v = dx/dt = −aω sin(ωt). Then v² = a²ω² sin²(ωt) = ω²[a² − a² cos²(ωt)] = ω²(a² − x²). The maximum speed is aω (at x = 0), and since the acceleration is −ω²x, the maximum acceleration is aω² (at the extremes x = ±a).

subjective.question: A particle of mass m moves under a force F in the xy-plane, so that at any time t its polar coordinates are (r, θ). Find the transverse component of the force.
subjective.answer: The transverse component of acceleration is r(d²θ/dt²) + 2(dr/dt)(dθ/dt), so the transverse component of force is: F_θ = m[r(d²θ/dt²) + 2(dr/dt)(dθ/dt)] This can also be written as F_θ = (m/r) · d/dt[r²(dθ/dt)]. In particular, if F_θ = 0, then r²(dθ/dt) remains constant during the motion.

subjective.question: Derive the radial and transverse components of the acceleration of a particle moving in a plane, in terms of its polar coordinates (r, θ).
subjective.answer: The position vector is r = r·e_r, where e_r and e_θ are unit vectors in the radial and transverse directions, with de_r/dt = (dθ/dt)e_θ and de_θ/dt = −(dθ/dt)e_r. Differentiating once: velocity = (dr/dt)e_r + r(dθ/dt)e_θ. Differentiating again and collecting components: Radial component of acceleration = d²r/dt² − r(dθ/dt)². Transverse component of acceleration = r(d²θ/dt²) + 2(dr/dt)(dθ/dt) = (1/r)·d/dt[r²(dθ/dt)].

subjective.question: A body of mass 2 kg is acted on by a horizontal force of magnitude 1/(2v + 1) N, where v is the velocity of the body (v > 0). The body starts from rest. Find the time at which the velocity is 1 m/s.
subjective.answer: By Newton's second law, m(dv/dt) = F, so: 2(dv/dt) = 1/(2v + 1) ⇒ dt = 2(2v + 1) dv. Integrating, with t = 0 when v = 0: t = ∫₀ᵛ 2(2u + 1) du = [2u² + 2u]₀ᵛ = 2v² + 2v. When v = 1 m/s: t = 2(1) + 2(1) = 4 s.
